## Introduction

In this post, I explore the `palmerpenguins` dataset using Python. I will use
pandas to answer two questions:

1. Which penguin has the highest bill length?
2. Which island has the most penguins?

## Loading the data and libraries

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins

penguins = load_penguins()

penguins.head()

```

## The data used in this analysis come from the
[Palmer Penguins dataset](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/),
collected by the Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.


## Which penguin has the highest bill length?
```{python} 
highest_bill = (
    penguins
    .sort_values("bill_length_mm", ascending=False)
    .head(1)
)

highest_bill
```

## 2. Number of penguins by island
```{python}
island_counts = (
    penguins
    .groupby("island")
    .size()
    .sort_values(ascending=False)
)

island_counts
```


```{python} 
#| label: fig-penguins-island
#| fig-cap: "Number of Penguins by Island"

island_counts.plot(
    kind="bar",
    title="Number of Penguins by Island",
    xlabel="Island",
    ylabel="Number of Penguins"
)

plt.xticks(rotation=0)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```



## 3. Average bill length by species

```{python}
#| label: fig-average-bill
#| fig-cap: "Average Bill Length by Species"

species_bill = penguins.groupby("species")["bill_length_mm"].mean()

species_bill.plot(
    kind="bar",
    color=["#4C78A8", "#F58518", "#54A24B"],
    title="Average Bill Length by Species",
    xlabel="Species",
    ylabel="Average Bill Length (mm)"
)

plt.xticks(rotation=0)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

```

## Number of Penguins by Species
```{python}
#| label: fig-penguins-species
#| fig-cap: "Number of Penguins by Species"


species_counts = penguins["species"].value_counts()

species_counts.plot(
    kind="bar",
    title="Number of Penguins by Species",
    xlabel="Species",
    ylabel="Number of Penguins"
)

plt.xticks(rotation=0)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Body Mass by Species
```{python}
#| label: fig-body-mass
#| fig-cap: "Body Mass by Species"

penguins.boxplot(
    column="body_mass_g",
    by="species",
    patch_artist=True
)

plt.title("Body Mass by Species")
plt.suptitle("")
plt.xlabel("Species")
plt.ylabel("Body Mass (g)")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

```

## Relationship between the Bill Length and Body Mass of Penguins by their Species
```{python} 
#| label: fig-bill-body-mass
#| fig-cap: "Relationship between Bill Length and Body Mass by Species"



plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))

for species in penguins["species"].dropna().unique():
    data = penguins[penguins["species"] == species]

    plt.scatter(
        data["bill_length_mm"],
        data["body_mass_g"],
        label=species,
        alpha=0.7
    )

plt.title("Bill Length vs Body Mass")
plt.xlabel("Bill Length (mm)")
plt.ylabel("Body Mass (g)")
plt.legend(title="Species")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

```
